items.title: Bug: Message creation accepts client-controlled id field
items.body:
### Bug Description
`POST /api/messages` forwards the request body directly into `sendMessage()`. The message service currently constructs records as `{ id: generated, ...payload, sentAt }`, so a caller can provide an `id` field and override the server-generated message id.

### Expected Behavior
Message ids should be server-owned. Client-controlled `id` values should be ignored so callers cannot create messages with arbitrary, duplicate, or misleading identifiers.

### Reproduction
1. Start the API.
2. Send `POST /api/messages` with `{ "id": "msg_attacker_controlled", "content": "hello", "recipientId": "usr_123" }`.
3. Observe that the response returns the caller-supplied id instead of a server-generated one.

### Proposed Fix
- Assign the generated `id` after spreading caller payload fields.
- Add a regression test proving caller-controlled `id` is ignored.

Parent bounty: #743

items.title: Message creation should ignore client supplied ids
items.body:
Parent bounty: #743

## Bug

`sendMessage()` currently creates new message records as:

```js
const message = { id: `msg_${Date.now()}`, ...payload, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() };
```

Because the untrusted payload is spread after the server-generated `id`, a client-provided `id` overwrites the message id. This lets callers create messages whose identifiers are controlled by the request body instead of the service-owned `msg_<timestamp>` value.

## Expected behavior

Message creation should ignore any client-supplied `id` and always preserve the server-generated message id, while keeping legitimate message fields and the server-owned `sentAt` timestamp intact.

## Scope

Keep the fix limited to message creation and add a regression test proving a client-controlled `id` cannot override the generated message id.

items.title: fix(api): validate message receiver exists before sending
items.body:
## Description

The `sendMessage` service does not validate that the `receiverId` corresponds to an existing user. This allows sending messages to non-existent users, creating orphaned messages in the system.

## Current Behavior

```javascript
export async function sendMessage(payload) {
  const message = { id: `msg_${Date.now()}`, ...payload, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() };
  messages.push(message);
  return message;
}
```

The `receiverId` from the payload is accepted without any existence check. An attacker could:
1. Send messages to random/non-existent user IDs
2. Flood the system with garbage messages referencing invalid users

## Expected Behavior

Validate that `receiverId` corresponds to an existing user before creating the message. Return a 404 error if the receiver does not exist.

## Impact
- Data integrity issues with orphaned messages
- Potential enumeration vector (though IDs are timestamp-based)
- Easy way to pollute the message store with invalid references

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.
/bounty $50

items.title: Message and job creation allow client-controlled field injection via object spread (Yzgaming005)
items.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

sendMessage() and createJob() use object spread (...payload) after setting the id field, allowing clients to override server-generated fields like id, status, and sentAt.

### Affected Files

- apps/api/src/services/messageService.js (line 8)
- apps/api/src/services/jobService.js (line 8)

### Reproduction

```sh
# Override the message id and sentAt
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/messages \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"content":"hello","id":"msg_INJECTED","sentAt":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
```

The server returns:
```json
{
  "id": "msg_INJECTED",
  "content": "hello",
  "sentAt": "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

The server-generated id and sentAt are overwritten by client input.

### Same bug in jobService.js

```sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/jobs \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"title":"test","id":"job_INJECTED","status":"closed"}'
```

Returns id: "job_INJECTED" and status: "closed" instead of the server-assigned values.

### Fix

Move the spread before the server-controlled fields:

```js
// messageService.js
const message = { ...payload, id: `msg_${Date.now()}`, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() };

// jobService.js
const job = { ...payload, id: `job_${Date.now()}`, status: "open" };
```

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

Ref: #743

items.title: Message creation should validate required fields and preserve server-owned ids
items.body:
## Problem
`POST /api/messages` currently forwards `req.body` directly into `sendMessage()`. This accepts incomplete message payloads with missing required fields from the message model such as `senderId`, `receiverId`, and `body`. The service also creates a server id and then spreads the caller payload afterward, so a request body can overwrite the generated `msg_*` id.

## Expected behavior
- Add a focused message creation validator.
- Require `senderId`, `receiverId`, and `body` before writing to the service layer.
- Return a structured `400` response for invalid message payloads.
- Preserve the generated `msg_*` id even if callers submit an `id` field.
- Add route/service regression coverage for missing receiver, blank body, and caller-supplied id overrides.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

- Existing domain payload fields should still be preserved.

items.title: Message and job creation allow client-controlled field injection via object spread (Yzgaming005)
items.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

sendMessage() and createJob() use object spread (...payload) after setting the id field, allowing clients to override server-generated fields like id, status, and sentAt.

### Affected Files

- apps/api/src/services/messageService.js (line 8)
- apps/api/src/services/jobService.js (line 8)

### Reproduction

```sh
# Override the message id and sentAt
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/messages \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"content":"hello","id":"msg_INJECTED","sentAt":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
```

The server returns:
```json
{
  "id": "msg_INJECTED",
  "content": "hello",
  "sentAt": "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

The server-generated id and sentAt are overwritten by client input.

### Same bug in jobService.js

```sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/jobs \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"title":"test","id":"job_INJECTED","status":"closed"}'
```

Returns id: "job_INJECTED" and status: "closed" instead of the server-assigned values.

### Fix

Move the spread before the server-controlled fields:

```js
// messageService.js
const message = { ...payload, id: `msg_${Date.now()}`, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() };

// jobService.js
const job = { ...payload, id: `job_${Date.now()}`, status: "open" };
```

items.title: Message creation allows caller-controlled read state and non-schema timestamp
items.body:
## Bug Description

`sendMessage()` currently builds new messages from the caller payload and then appends a `sentAt` timestamp. This makes the in-memory message service diverge from the Prisma `Message` model shape: new messages do not get an explicit unread default, and they use a non-schema `sentAt` field instead of `createdAt`.

Because the payload is spread directly, a caller can also submit `isRead: true` and make a newly-created message appear already read.

## Reproduction

Call the message service with a normal message payload:

```js
await sendMessage({
  senderId: "usr_sender",
  receiverId: "usr_receiver",
  body: "hello"
});
```

The returned message has `sentAt`, no `createdAt`, and no explicit `isRead: false`.

Then call it with caller-controlled read state:

```js
await sendMessage({
  senderId: "usr_sender",
  receiverId: "usr_receiver",
  body: "hello",
  isRead: true
});
```

The service preserves the caller-supplied `isRead: true` value.

## Expected Behavior

New messages should be schema-shaped and server-owned defaults should win:

- `isRead: false` for all newly-created messages.
- `createdAt` should be populated with an ISO timestamp.
- `sentAt` should not be emitted by the service.
- caller-supplied `isRead` and `sentAt` should be ignored on create.

## Proposed Fix

Strip caller-controlled `isRead` and `sentAt` fields from the payload before storing the message, then add server-owned `isRead: false` and `createdAt` values. Add focused service tests covering the default and override paths.

Refs #743.

- `createdAt` is populated with an ISO timestamp.
- The non-schema `sentAt` field is not emitted.

duplicate_candidates.title: Message and job creation allow client-controlled field injection via object spread (Yzgaming005)
duplicate_candidates.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

sendMessage() and createJob() use object spread (...payload) after setting the id field, allowing clients to override server-generated fields like id, status, and sentAt.

### Affected Files

- apps/api/src/services/messageService.js (line 8)
- apps/api/src/services/jobService.js (line 8)

### Reproduction

```sh
# Override the message id and sentAt
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/messages \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"content":"hello","id":"msg_INJECTED","sentAt":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
```

The server returns:
```json
{
  "id": "msg_INJECTED",
  "content": "hello",
  "sentAt": "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

The server-generated id and sentAt are overwritten by client input.

### Same bug in jobService.js

```sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/jobs \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"title":"test","id":"job_INJECTED","status":"closed"}'
```

Returns id: "job_INJECTED" and status: "closed" instead of the server-assigned values.

### Fix

Move the spread before the server-controlled fields:

```js
// messageService.js
const message = { ...payload, id: `msg_${Date.now()}`, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() };

// jobService.js
const job = { ...payload, id: `job_${Date.now()}`, status: "open" };
```

## Bug

`apps/api/src/services/messageService.js` stores messages in a module-level in-memory array, but `listMessages()` returns that backing array directly and `sendMessage()` returns the same object reference that was stored. - Existing payload fields and `sentAt` behavior should otherwise remain unchanged.

strong_duplicates.title: Message and job creation allow client-controlled field injection via object spread (Yzgaming005)
strong_duplicates.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

sendMessage() and createJob() use object spread (...payload) after setting the id field, allowing clients to override server-generated fields like id, status, and sentAt.

### Affected Files

- apps/api/src/services/messageService.js (line 8)
- apps/api/src/services/jobService.js (line 8)

### Reproduction

```sh
# Override the message id and sentAt
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/messages \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"content":"hello","id":"msg_INJECTED","sentAt":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"}'
```

The server returns:
```json
{
  "id": "msg_INJECTED",
  "content": "hello",
  "sentAt": "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

The server-generated id and sentAt are overwritten by client input.

### Same bug in jobService.js

```sh
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/jobs \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"title":"test","id":"job_INJECTED","status":"closed"}'
```

Returns id: "job_INJECTED" and status: "closed" instead of the server-assigned values.

### Fix

Move the spread before the server-controlled fields:

```js
// messageService.js
const message = { ...payload, id: `msg_${Date.now()}`, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() };

// jobService.js
const job = { ...payload, id: `job_${Date.now()}`, status: "open" };
```

## Bug

`createNotification()` in `apps/api/src/services/notificationService.js` spreads the caller payload after the server-assigned fields:

```js
export async function createNotification(payload) {
  const notification = { id: `ntf_${Date.now()}`, read: false, ...payload };
```

items.title: Create services should return defensive record snapshots
items.body:
Parent bounty: #743
Original issue: #3218

## Bug
The in-memory create service functions store a record and return the same object reference to the caller. If the caller mutates the returned record after creation, the backing store changes without going through a service method.

Affected examples include `createJob()`, `createProposal()`, `createReview()`, `sendMessage()`, `createNotification()`, and `createUser()`.

## Expected behavior
Create services should store a snapshot of the new record and return a separate response snapshot. Array fields should also be copied so later mutations of the original payload or returned response do not alter stored service state.

## Scope
- Return defensive snapshots from create service functions.
- Store defensive snapshots so later mutations of original payload arrays cannot alter service state.
- Add focused service tests for returned-record mutation and payload-array mutation.
- Do not change list-service behavior, route auth, validation, persistence, or generated ID rules.

items.title: Service-generated ids should be collision-resistant and server-owned
items.body:
Parent Algora bounty: #743

## Bug
Several API services generate public record identifiers with `Date.now()`. Records created in the same millisecond can receive duplicate ids even though they are distinct records. Some create paths also spread caller payloads after server-owned fields, which lets request bodies override fields such as `id`, `status`, `read`, or `sentAt`.

Affected examples include registration/user, job, message, notification, payment, proposal, and review service creation paths.

## Impact
Duplicate or caller-controlled ids can confuse downstream lookups, collide with existing records, and break the assumption that service-created resources own their identifiers and lifecycle fields. Registration also needs one generated user id reused for both the API response and JWT `sub` claim.

## Expected behavior
- Preserve existing id prefixes while using collision-resistant ids.
- Reuse the generated registration id in the access-token subject.
- Apply service-owned fields after caller payload fields so submitted payloads cannot override them.
- Add focused service-level regression coverage for same-millisecond uniqueness and server-owned field override attempts.

## Scope
Keep the change limited to API service id generation and focused tests. Do not change persistence, routing, auth policy, payment provider behavior, or frontend UI.

## Bug

`POST /api/notifications` lets a direct caller create a notification that is already marked as read. `apps/api/src/services/notificationService.js` builds the new object with `read: false` before spreading the caller payload:

- Apply caller payload fields first, then apply server-owned `id` and `read: false` after the payload.
- Add focused regression tests for default unread status and caller-supplied `read: true` override prevention.
- Keep the change scoped to notification creation behavior.

items.title: HIGH: Missing Input Validation on 6 API Controllers Enables Arbitrary Data Submission
items.body:
## Description

Six API controllers in `apps/api/src/controllers/` accept `req.body` directly without any schema validation (Zod or otherwise). This means an attacker can send arbitrary, malformed, or malicious data to these endpoints, and it will be stored and processed without any structural validation.

## Affected Controllers

| Controller File | Endpoint | Unvalidated Input |
|----------------|----------|-------------------|
| `proposalController.js` | POST /api/proposals | `req.body` â€” cover letter, bid amount, job ID, freelancer ID |
| `messageController.js` | POST /api/messages | `req.body` â€” message body, sender, receiver |
| `reviewController.js` | POST /api/reviews | `req.body` â€” rating, comment, reviewer, reviewee |
| `userController.js` | POST /api/users | `req.body` â€” full user creation payload |
| `notificationController.js` | POST /api/notifications | `req.body` â€” user ID, title, body |
| `paymentController.js` | POST /api/payments | `req.body` â€” amount, currency, provider |

Compare with `authController.js` which DOES use proper validation:
```js
const payload = registerSchema.parse(req.body);  // Validated
```

And `jobController.js` which also validates:
```js
const payload = createJobSchema.parse(req.body);  // Validated
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Send a POST request to any affected endpoint with malformed data:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/proposals \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bogusField": true, "malicious": "<script>alert(1)</script>"}'
```
2. The server accepts the data and returns HTTP 201 without throwing any validation error
3. The data is stored in the in-memory array and may be served back via the GET endpoint

## Impact

**High (CVSS 7.5)** â€” Data integrity and injection risks:
- Malformed data is accepted without validation
- Potential for stored XSS if the data is later rendered in the frontend
- Business logic bypass (setting arbitrary amounts, ratings, user associations)
- No type enforcement on critical fields (amounts, user IDs, ratings)

## Recommended Fix

Add Zod validation schemas for each controller following the pattern in `jobController.js`:

```js
// Example for proposalController.js
import { z } from "zod";

const createProposalSchema = z.object({
  jobId: z.string().min(1),
  coverLetter: z.string().min(10),
  bidAmount: z.number().positive(),
  estDuration: z.string().min(1)
});
```

items.title: Create services should return defensive record snapshots
items.body:
Parent bounty: #743
Original issue: #3218

## Bug
The in-memory create service functions store a record and return the same object reference to the caller. If the caller mutates the returned record after creation, the backing store changes without going through a service method.

Affected examples include `createJob()`, `createProposal()`, `createReview()`, `sendMessage()`, `createNotification()`, and `createUser()`.

## Expected behavior
Create services should store a snapshot of the new record and return a separate response snapshot. Array fields should also be copied so later mutations of the original payload or returned response do not alter stored service state.

## Scope
- Return defensive snapshots from create service functions.
- Store defensive snapshots so later mutations of original payload arrays cannot alter service state.
- Add focused service tests for returned-record mutation and payload-array mutation.
- Do not change list-service behavior, route auth, validation, persistence, or generated ID rules.

duplicate_candidates.title: Proposal creation should not allow caller-controlled ids
duplicate_candidates.body:
## Bug

`POST /api/proposals` lets a caller override the server-generated proposal id. `apps/api/src/services/proposalService.js` creates the proposal object with `id` first, then spreads the caller payload afterward:

```js
const proposal = { id: `prp_${Date.now()}`, ...payload };
```

Because the payload is applied after the generated id, a request body can replace the server-owned proposal id.

Reproduction payload:

```json
{
  "id": "prp_attacker",
  "jobId": "job_1",
  "freelancerId": "usr_1",
  "coverLetter": "Hello"
}
```

Observed behavior from current `origin/main`:

```text
HTTP 201
{ "success": true, "data": { "id": "prp_attacker", "jobId": "job_1", "freelancerId": "usr_1", "coverLetter": "Hello" } }
```

## Impact

- Public proposal creation can choose a server-owned identifier.
- Callers can create confusing or colliding proposal ids.
- Downstream workflow that trusts proposal ids can be associated with client-controlled identifiers.

## Expected behavior

The server should always own the generated proposal id. Caller-supplied `id` values should not override the generated `prp_...` value, while normal proposal payload fields should still be preserved.

## Proposed fix

- Apply caller payload fields before server-owned fields in proposal creation.
- Add endpoint regression coverage proving caller-supplied `id` is ignored.
- Keep the change scoped to proposal creation behavior.

items.title: fix(api): review creation should verify reviewer identity from auth token
items.body:
## Description

The `POST /api/reviews` endpoint accepts a `reviewerId` from the request body without verifying it matches the authenticated user. An attacker can impersonate any user when creating reviews.

## Current Behavior

```javascript
// reviewRoutes.js
reviewRoutes.get("/", getReviews);
reviewRoutes.post("/", postReview);  // No auth check on reviewerId
```

The `createReview` service accepts `reviewerId` directly from the payload with no validation:

```javascript
export async function createReview(payload) {
  const review = { id: `rev_${Date.now()}`, ...payload };
  reviews.push(review);
  return review;
}
```

## Expected Behavior
1. Add auth middleware to POST /api/reviews
2. Override `reviewerId` with `req.user.sub` from the JWT token
3. Validate that `revieweeId` exists

## Impact
- Review forgery and impersonation
- Trust/reputation system compromise
- Easy to artificially inflate or deflate user ratings

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

items.title: Review service should generate collision-resistant ids (Lynn-Lee reissue via #743)
items.body:
Parent Algora bounty: #743

## Bug

`apps/api/src/services/reviewService.js` generates review ids with `Date.now()`:

```js
const review = { id: `rev_${Date.now()}`, ...payload };
```

That makes review ids predictable and can produce collisions when two reviews are created within the same millisecond.

## Steps to reproduce

Freeze the clock and call the service twice:

```js
Date.now = () => 1720000000000;
await createReview({ reviewerId: "usr_a", revieweeId: "usr_b", rating: 5, comment: "fast" });
await createReview({ reviewerId: "usr_c", revieweeId: "usr_d", rating: 4, comment: "clear" });
```

## Expected behavior

Each new review should receive a collision-resistant server-generated id even when records are created in the same millisecond.

## Actual behavior

Both reviews can receive the same `rev_1720000000000` id.

## Suggested fix

Replace the timestamp-only id generation with a collision-resistant server-owned id such as `crypto.randomUUID()` while preserving the existing `rev_` prefix.

## Validation plan

- Add a focused `reviewService` regression test that freezes `Date.now()` and asserts distinct ids across rapid creates.
- Run `node --test apps/api/src/tests/reviewService.test.js`.
- Run `node --test apps/api/src/tests/*.test.js`.

## Safety

No payout, contact, credential, wallet, or off-platform payment details should be posted publicly.

Refs #743 and #1283.

items.title: Review service should generate collision-resistant ids (Lynn-Lee reissue via #743)
items.body:
Parent Algora bounty: #743

## Bug

`apps/api/src/services/reviewService.js` generates review ids with `Date.now()`:

```js
const review = { id: `rev_${Date.now()}`, ...payload };
```

That makes review ids predictable and can produce collisions when two reviews are created within the same millisecond.

## Steps to reproduce

Freeze the clock and call the service twice:

```js
Date.now = () => 1720000000000;
await createReview({ reviewerId: "usr_a", revieweeId: "usr_b", rating: 5, comment: "fast" });
await createReview({ reviewerId: "usr_c", revieweeId: "usr_d", rating: 4, comment: "clear" });
```

## Expected behavior

Each new review should receive a collision-resistant server-generated id even when records are created in the same millisecond.

## Actual behavior

Both reviews can receive the same `rev_1720000000000` id.

## Suggested fix

Replace the timestamp-only id generation with a collision-resistant server-owned id such as `crypto.randomUUID()` while preserving the existing `rev_` prefix.

## Validation plan

- Add a focused `reviewService` regression test that freezes `Date.now()` and asserts distinct ids across rapid creates.
- Run `node --test apps/api/src/tests/reviewService.test.js`.
- Run `node --test apps/api/src/tests/*.test.js`.

## Safety

No payout, contact, credential, wallet, or off-platform payment details should be posted publicly.

Refs #743 and #1283.

duplicate_candidates.body:
## Bug

`POST /api/reviews` lets a caller override the server-generated review id. `apps/api/src/services/reviewService.js` creates the review object with `id` first, then spreads the caller payload afterward:

```js
const review = { id: `rev_${Date.now()}`, ...payload };
```

```json
}

```

- Public review creation can choose a server-owned identifier.
- Callers can create confusing or colliding review ids.
- Downstream review lookups or audit trails can be associated with client-controlled identifiers.

## Expected behavior

The server should always own the generated review id. Caller-supplied `id` values should not override the generated `rev_...` value, while normal review payload fields should still be preserved.

## Proposed fix

strong_duplicates.title: Review service should generate collision-resistant server-owned ids
strong_duplicates.body:
## Bug

`apps/api/src/services/reviewService.js` generates review ids with a timestamp-only value:

```js
const review = { id: `rev_${Date.now()}`, ...payload };
```

That can produce duplicate review ids when two reviews are created in the same millisecond. It also lets a client-provided `id` override the server-generated id because `...payload` is spread after `id`.

## Steps to reproduce

Freeze the clock and create two reviews:

```js
Date.now = () => 1720000000000;
await createReview({ reviewerId: "usr_a", revieweeId: "usr_b", rating: 5, comment: "fast" });
await createReview({ reviewerId: "usr_c", revieweeId: "usr_d", rating: 4, comment: "clear" });
```

## Expected behavior

Each new review should receive a unique, server-owned id even when records are created in the same millisecond. The existing `rev_` prefix should be preserved.

## Scope

- Replace timestamp-only review id generation with a collision-resistant server-owned id.
- Add a focused `reviewService` regression test that freezes `Date.now()` and asserts two rapid creates have distinct `rev_` ids.
- Verify client-supplied `id` cannot override the server-owned id.

Refs #743 and #10850.

strong_duplicates.body:
Parent bounty: #743

## Summary

`createReview` currently trusts fields from `req.body` when building the review record:

```bash
node --test src/tests/*.test.js
```

## Problem
`POST /api/users` currently forwards `req.body` directly into `createUser()`. The service creates users with `{ id: `usr_${Date.now()}`, ...payload }`, so client input can override the generated user ID and empty payloads can be stored as users.

- Add a dedicated user validator.
- Require `email` and `name`, with `role` defaulting to `client`.
- Return HTTP 400 for invalid user input.
- Pass only parsed fields into the service so `id` remains server-controlled.
- Cover empty payload, attempted `id` override, and role defaulting with API tests.

## Non-overlap
This is user-route validation and server-owned identity only. It does not overlap with auth registration role, message payload, review rating, proposal validation, notification validation, auth, upload, admin metrics, JWT secret, payment gateway, or job budget validation issues.

items.title: User and proposal creation should keep generated ids server-owned (SnowfallHD reissue via #743)
items.body:
### Bug Description
`POST /api/users` and `POST /api/proposals` forward request bodies into services that construct records as `{ id: generated, ...payload }`. Because caller payload fields are spread last, a client can provide an `id` field and override the server-generated user or proposal id.

### Expected Behavior
User and proposal ids should be server-owned. Client-controlled `id` values should be ignored so callers cannot create records with arbitrary, duplicate, or misleading identifiers.

### Reproduction
1. Start the API.

items.title: Bug: createUser mass assignment allows setting arbitrary user fields including role
items.body:
## Bug

`POST /api/users` calls `createUser(req.body)` which spreads `...payload` directly into the user object. This allows callers to set any field, including `role: "admin"`, `isAdmin: true`, or other sensitive properties.

## Reproduction

1. Start the API server
2. Send `POST /api/users` with body:
```json
{"name": "attacker", "email": "evil@test.com", "role": "admin", "isAdmin": true, "balance": 999999}
```

The endpoint should only accept whitelisted fields (name, email, password) and reject or ignore any additional fields.

- Privilege escalation: any user can make themselves admin
- Data injection: arbitrary fields stored in user records
- No input validation on user creation

## Proposed fix

- Use a Zod schema to validate and strip unknown fields
- Only allow safe fields: name, email, password
- Add tests for field restriction

strong_duplicates.title: User creation accepts empty payloads and client-controlled IDs
strong_duplicates.body:
This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

## Problem
`POST /api/users` currently forwards `req.body` directly into `createUser()`. The service creates users with `{ id: `usr_${Date.now()}`, ...payload }`, so client input can override the generated user ID and empty payloads can be stored as users.

## Reproduction
Send this payload to `/api/users`:

```json
{
  "id": "usr_attacker",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "name": "Example User",
  "role": "client"
}
```

Expected: the API should ignore or reject client-controlled `id` and create a server-generated `usr_` ID.
Actual: because the payload is spread after the generated `id`, the stored user can use the caller-provided `id`.

An empty `{}` payload is also accepted instead of returning HTTP 400.

## Impact
User records become untrustworthy because callers can create incomplete users or choose identifiers that should be server-owned. Any downstream lookup, audit, or relationship mapping that relies on `id` integrity can be affected.

## Proposed fix
- Add a dedicated user validator.
- Require `email` and `name`, with `role` defaulting to `client`.
- Return HTTP 400 for invalid user input.
- Pass only parsed fields into the service so `id` remains server-controlled.
- Cover empty payload, attempted `id` override, and role defaulting with API tests.

## Non-overlap
This is user-route validation and server-owned identity only. It does not overlap with auth registration role, message payload, review rating, proposal validation, notification validation, auth, upload, admin metrics, JWT secret, payment gateway, or job budget validation issues.
